description: A composite group of two unlabelled panels: a rendered data table (left) and a grouped bar chart (right), both reporting Vickers microhardness of Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe as-cast low-density steels. The table columns are Samples, Matrix (Austenite) hardness (HV), Error, Ferrite hardness (HV), Error, Be-Fe phase hardness (HV), Error, with rows 0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be. Austenite hardness increases steadily: 453.31 ±11.34 HV (0Be), 462.88 ±13.84 (0.5Be), 475.80 ±13.75 (1.0Be), 479.74 ±11.99 HV (1.5Be). Ferrite and Be-Fe phase cells are dashes for 0Be and 0.5Be; 1.0Be lists ferrite 437.40 ±15.72 and Be-Fe phase 483.50 ±16.65 HV; 1.5Be lists 452.54 ±12.33 and 477.16 ±14.14 HV. The bar chart plots Hardness (HV) on y (0–600, ticks every 100) against the four Be contents on x, legend red = Austenite and blue = Ferrite. Only 0Be and 0.5Be have a single red bar; 1.0Be and 1.5Be show red-blue pairs. Every bar is labelled with its value (453.31, 462.88, 475.80, 437.40, 479.74, 452.54) and carries an error bar. No Be-Fe phase bars are plotted. The group demonstrates that Be addition raises austenite hardness and that ferrite (present only in 1.0Be and 1.5Be) is softer than austenite.

subfigures.description: Data table with columns Samples, Matrix (Austenite) hardness (HV), Error, Ferrite hardness (HV), Error, Be-Fe phase hardness (HV), Error; rows 0Be (453.31 ±11.34 HV, other entries '-'), 0.5Be (462.88 ±13.84 HV, other entries '-'), 1.0Be (475.80 ±13.75, 437.40 ±15.72, 483.50 ±16.65 HV) and 1.5Be (479.74 ±11.99, 452.54 ±12.33, 477.16 ±14.14 HV).

Grouped column chart of Hardness (HV) on the y-axis (0–600) versus sample 0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be, 1.5Be on the x-axis; legend: red = Austenite, blue = Ferrite. 0Be and 0.5Be show only a red Austenite bar; 1.0Be and 1.5Be show paired red Austenite and blue Ferrite bars. Each bar is annotated with its numeric hardness value and has an error bar; the chart shows no Be-Fe phase bars.

observations.observation: The group consists of two panels of different kinds: a rendered data table and a grouped bar chart, both giving Vickers hardness (HV) for the same four alloys.
The table lists austenite hardness values 453.31 ±11.34 HV (0Be), 462.88 ±13.84 HV (0.5Be), 475.80 ±13.75 HV (1.0Be) and 479.74 ±11.99 HV (1.5Be), i.e. a monotonic increase with Be content.
Ferrite hardness is only tabulated for the Be-containing dual-phase steels: 437.40 ±15.72 HV (1.0Be) and 452.54 ±12.33 HV (1.5Be); the 0Be and 0.5Be ferrite cells read '-'.
Be-Fe phase hardness is tabulated as 483.50 ±16.65 HV (1.0Be) and 477.16 ±14.14 HV (1.5Be), while the 0Be and 0.5Be Be-Fe phase cells read '-' and their Error cells are blank.
The bar chart y-axis is labelled 'Hardness (HV)' with ticks from 0 to 600 in steps of 100; the x-axis gives the categorical sample labels 0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be, 1.5Be.
The bar chart legend has two entries: red = Austenite and blue = Ferrite; 0Be and 0.5Be show only the red Austenite bar, whereas 1.0Be and 1.5Be show one red and one blue bar each.
Printed above the bars are the values 453.31, 462.88, 475.80 and 437.40, 479.74 and 452.54, matching the table's austenite and ferrite hardness numbers; every bar also shows an error bar.
The bar chart contains no bar for the Be-Fe phase, so the Be-Fe hardness values present in the table are not displayed graphically.
The caption describes the group as microhardness of Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe low-density as-cast steels and titles the figure 'Microhardness of as-cast austenite of experimental steels'.
The citing text states that hardness of the austenite matrix increases with increasing beryllium content.

The citing text states that the ferrite hardness also increases with Be content in the 1.0Be and 1.5Be steels, and that ferrite hardness is lower than austenite hardness — consistent with the tabulated and plotted values.
The citing text states that 0Be and 0.5Be steels are fully austenitic with no ferrite hardness values, while 1.0Be and 1.5Be are ferrite + austenite dual-phase steels.

The citing text states that because of a problem with the hardness tester the Be–Fe phase hardness could not be tested in the 0.5Be steel, which matches the '-' entry in the table and its absence from the chart.
